questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem:
Farida sews footballs in her room in Ludhiana every day. An MNC in a developed country places orders for production with small producers like her, and the footballs leave her hands without her ever knowing the label they will carry, because the MNC sells them under its own brand name. Farida has no say in what her work is worth: the MNC has tremendous power to determine price, quality, delivery and labour conditions for producers working at such a distance. Meanwhile, Cargill now controls the four oil refineries that once belonged to Parakh Foods, and makes 5 million pouches of edible oil every day.

(a) Farida sews footballs in her room in Ludhiana for a big company in another country. Why does a company in a developed country place orders for production with producers like Farida, and what happens to the footballs after they leave her hands? (b) Name the four things that company has tremendous power to determine for producers working at such a distance. (c) Farida never meets the firm that buys her footballs, and the label on them is not hers. Analyse what her experience shows about who really decides the price, the quality and the labour conditions of goods made thousands of kilometres away from the market.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: (a) Large MNCs in developed countries place orders for production with small producers, and the products are supplied to them and sold under their own brand names. (b) Price, quality, delivery and labour conditions. (c) The MNCs decide, because they place the orders and sell the goods under their own brand names, and they have tremendous power over these distant producers.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem:
Until recently the edible oil on Indian shop shelves came from Parakh Foods, a firm that had built a large marketing network in various parts of India, where its brand was well-reputed. Control of its four oil refineries has now shifted elsewhere. The firm that has taken over is today the largest producer of edible oil in India, with a capacity to make 5 million pouches daily. Firms of this kind are among the top MNCs, and many of the top MNCs have wealth exceeding the entire budgets of the developing country governments.

(a) Name the firm whose four oil refineries have changed hands, and say which firm controls them now and what that firm produces. (b) How many oil refineries did the first firm own, and what kind of business had it built in the different parts of India? (c) Anil has heard that many of the top MNCs have wealth exceeding the entire budgets of the developing country governments. Analyse what power and influence wealth of that kind lets them exercise over production in countries far from their own.

(b) Four oil refineries and a large marketing network in various parts of India. (c) Such wealth brings power and influence: they use local companies for supplies, compete closely with them or buy them up, and so influence production far away.
